description: Intent i002 (alloc-multiply-overflow, snapshot s01) complete. FINDING (medium confidence): drivers/virt/fsl_hypervisor.c:218-240, ioctl_memcpy (FSL_HV_IOCTL_MEMCPY on /dev/fsl-hv). Untrusted source: userspace u64 param.count via copy_from_user (line 165). Violated invariant: num_pages declared 'unsigned int' (line 155) is assigned (param.count + lb_offset + PAGE_SIZE - 1) >> PAGE_SHIFT (line 221) — the 64-bit sum truncates to 32 bits with only a u64-wraparound check at 218-219, no upper clamp — and the allocation 'kmalloc(num_pages * sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) + sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) - 1, GFP_KERNEL)' (lines 239-240) is a plain 32-bit multiply-add with no overflow-checked sizing (struct fh_sg_list = 32 bytes, arch/powerpc/include/asm/fsl_hcalls.h:341-346). Unsafe use: fill loop 'for (i = 1; i < num_pages; i++)' (line 274) writes sg_list[i].source/.target/.size (lines 277-287) for all num_pages entries; num_pages=2^27 wraps the product to 0 so kmalloc(31) succeeds and the loop writes gigabytes past the heap buffer — the seed's truncated-multiply -> undersized-alloc -> element-indexed-write chain under an outside-the-kernel count. Within-function asymmetric hardening: the sibling 'pages = kzalloc_objs(struct page *, num_pages)' (line 229) sizes via size_mul (include/linux/slab.h:971-975), overflow-checked, while the S/G list buffer is not. Seed family verified PATCHED in s01 (usbip_common.c:685 clamp, :699 kcalloc) and excluded by rule. Limitations: ripgrep PATH resolution failed so the broad allocator-adjacent multiply sweeps over drivers/fs/net/sound/block/crypto were not executed — the audit is bounded to the deep-read chain plus the seed check; exploitation requires get_user_pages_fast to pin exactly num_pages pages (line 249-256, ~512GB for the wrap case) and access to the powerpc-specific /dev/fsl-hv node; no runtime reproducer was built.
